title: Tessera open-source dashboard for Home Assistant runs on ESP32 touchscreen devkits
summary:
The open-source Tessera project enables neat dashboards for Home Assistant on affordable 2.8-inch to 10.1-inch ESP32 touchscreen (development) kits from CYD, Guition, and Waveshare. The Tessera firmware adds a layer to ESPHome firmware for display management, touchscreen handling, dashboard rendering, tiles, plugins, and more. It works in conjunction with the Tessera Screen Manager, which provides the Home Assistant interface to configure screens, manage layouts, install firmware, and push updates. The whole solution is supposed to be easy to use thanks to a drag-and-drop editor, and users don’t need to know anything about YAML or MQTT. Tessera features highlights: Hardware support – Various ESP32 touchscreen platforms from 2.8-inch Cheap Yellow Displays (CYD) to 10.1-inch Guition panels. Drag-and-drop dashboard editor Configure screens, pages and tiles from Home Assistant. No YAML knowledge is needed. Multi-page dashboards – Organize controls across multiple pages Customizable layouts – Configure grid dimensions, tile sizes, icons, colours and [...]

title: Piccola CNC – An open-source hardware desktop milling machine with PCB auto-leveling and integrated CAM (Crowdfunding)
summary:
InMachines Ingrassia GmbH has launched the Piccola CNC, an open-source hardware desktop CNC milling machine designed for PCB prototyping and machining wood, plastics, and soft metals such as aluminum, brass, and copper. Built in Germany, the machine features a 150 × 150 × 70 mm work area, belt-driven ball screws on all three axes, ER11 collets, and a choice of 100W or 200W spindles. The machine comes in three versions, which include the Basic, Pro, and Ultimate. The Pro variant adds a full enclosure and safety interlocks, while the Ultimate model further adds a brushless spindle and laser distance sensor. Other features include USB-C and Wi-Fi connectivity, built-in CAM software for PCB, 2D, 3D, and rotary milling, and laser-based PCB height mapping on the Ultimate, with the sensor available as an accessory for Basic and Pro. title: AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 Series embedded processors offer up to 256 Zen 6c cores, PCIe Gen 6, and CXL 3.1
summary:
AMD has introduced the EPYC Embedded 9006 Series SP7, a family of high-performance x86 SoCs built around the Zen 6 and Zen 6c architectures using a 2nm CPU process. Designed for semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), networking appliances, firewalls, and enterprise storage controllers, the new embedded processors feature up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and 1GB of L3 cache, with power ratings ranging from 400W to 600W. Compared to the previous-generation EPYC Embedded 9005 Series, the new processors offer 16-channel DDR5 memory with RDIMM and MRDIMM support, up to 96 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, and CXL 3.1 connectivity. They also offer improved security, enterprise-class reliability, and seven-year product availability, making them suitable for long-lifecycle embedded systems.
